☕️ Good Monday afternoon. Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 659 words, a 2-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

⚡️ Situational awareness: President Trump told Axios in a phone interview today that he's "in no rush" to decide whether to resume fighting in Iran. More from Barak Ravid.
 
 
1 big thing: Supermarket hack attack
 
Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

Hackers are attacking supermarket fridge and freezer systems across Europe, raising concerns of similar episodes in the U.S., Axios' Herb Scribner reports.

👾 Dozens of European supermarkets were hit with suspected cyberattacks overnight, spoiling food and threatening costly losses.

  • Grocery chains Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt said incidents affected stores in Belgium and Luxembourg, Reuters reports.
  • Swedish chains ICA and Coop reported similar disruptions.

🇫🇷 The incidents follow similar attacks in France last month, where hackers seized control of hundreds of refrigeration units.

  • It's unclear whether the attacks are connected.
Workers empty spoiled frozen goods today at a supermarket in Sjöbo, Sweden. Photo: Johan Nilsson/TT News Agency via Getty Images

How it works: Many grocery stores use internet-connected devices, letting maintenance workers remotely monitor temperatures.

  • Hackers can exploit software flaws or stolen login credentials to change temperatures or activate defrost modes via those devices.

🥶 Many U.S. supermarkets use fridge and freezer units like those affected in Europe, raising concerns that they could be vulnerable to similar attacks.

  • The Pentagon is also investigating whether cyberattacks caused freezer malfunctions in at least six U.S. military commissaries in August.

What to know.
 
 
2. 🛡️ Trump vows to protect Elon
 
Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photos via Getty Images

President Trump says he'll try to protect Elon Musk if Democrats investigate the SpaceX and Tesla CEO after tomorrow's midterm elections, Axios' Ben Berkowitz reports.

  • Trump also suggested preemptive pardons for staff and others around him.

🎙️ In an interview for the "Pod Force One" podcast published early today, the New York Post's Miranda Devine asked Trump about rumors of Musk being investigated or having his assets seized.

  • Trump said: "It's talk. But if it is talk, we'll have to protect them."

🤑 Musk has spent nearly half a billion dollars opposing Democrats during this election cycle.

  • He also recently suggested that it would be the end of democracy if Democrats win the White House and Congress in 2028.

Trump also said that he'd consider pardons for his staff and other allies if Democrats pursue them: "I would not even think about it. I'd do it."

Helping America’s small businesses put AI to work

3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
Sen. Susan Collins campaigns today at Ellis Family Market in Patten, Maine. Photo: Taylor Coester/Reuters
  • 🗳️ 50 million Americans have already cast ballots in this week's midterm elections. There are some promising signs for Democrats, but it's too early to draw any big conclusions. Explore the data.
  • 🧑‍⚖️ A federal judge dismissed a complaint against two former FBI officials accused of covering up how much they knew about the investigation into a laptop reportedly tied to Hunter Biden. Go deeper.
  • 🌎 Ex-paratrooper Karl Bushby finished his 28-year odyssey of walking around the world today, returning to his mother's home in northern England for the first time since 1998. He told reporters that he depended on "the kindness of strangers, so many, from individuals to nation-states, to get me back here today." Go deeper.

4. 📸 Pic to go: Sign of the times
 
Photo: Luiz Rampelotto/EuropaNewswire via Reuters

Thousands of friends, family and spectators lined the course of yesterday's New York City Marathon to cheer on the approximately 60,000 runners from more than 140 countries.

  • It's one of the best days of the year in the Big Apple, with huge crowds supporting those undertaking the 26.2-mile gauntlet from Staten Island to Central Park via Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.

🍿 One popular sign this year: Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes promising the finish line is near and asking, "Why would I deceive you?" — a reference to the smash hit documentary, "You Can See Everything."
